plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: Pale lilac-pink goblets rise straight from bare ground, with no leaves in sight. They carpet damp meadows and light woodland edges like a scattering of tulips that came up out of season.
plants.location: Meadows and gardens across Europe, from the British Isles to central Europe
plants.funFact: The flowers bloom in autumn, but the leaves and seed capsules appear the following spring. Every part of the plant contains colchicine, a toxic compound that scientists use in plant breeding to double chromosome numbers.

plants.name: Aster novae-angliae
plants.description: Dense clusters of daisy-like blooms with golden centers and many narrow petals light up prairies, roadsides and gardens. Monarch butterflies stop here to feed on their long autumn migration.
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from New England to the Midwest prairies
plants.funFact: Its flower heads close up on cloudy days and at night, and open again in full sun. It is one of the most important late-season nectar sources for migrating monarchs.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: Branches are covered in fluffy, fragrant golden pom-poms that glow against blue-green foliage. Southern Australia's bushland turns sunny yellow as winter gives way to spring.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to mid-spring (roughly July to October)
plants.location: Southeastern and southern Australia, including Victoria, New South Wales and South Australia
plants.funFact: It is Australia's national floral emblem. National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1, the first day of spring.
